title: Molecular Shell Corrosion Analysis Lab
description: You are a materials chemist analyzing how acidic ocean environments corrode protective nacre coatings. The IridescenceAbalone represents a pristine calcium carbonate shell sample, while the DamagedHelmet represents a corroded metal substrate exposed after shell degradation. The user must run a multi-step titration experiment, adjusting pH levels and reagent concentrations to study and reverse the corrosion process.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a chemistry corrosion analysis lab. Load IridescenceAbalone.glb (positioned left, representing a nacre/CaCO3 shell sample) and DamagedHelmet.glb (positioned right, representing corroded metal substrate). Use GLTFLoader and OrbitControls. Set up a dark lab environment with a subtle ambient light (0x334455) and two point lights simulating lab lamps. Camera starts at (0, 2, 5) looking at origin. Create an HTML overlay panel with these interactive controls: (1) A pH slider (range 1-14, default 7) that when adjusted below 4 causes the abalone shell to gradually become transparent (opacity reduction) simulating acid dissolution of CaCO3, and above 10 causes a blue glow emission on the shell simulating alkaline re-mineralization. (2) A 'Reagent Concentration' slider (0-100%) that scales a visible particle system (small spheres) flowing between the two models representing chemical reagent molecules. (3) A 'Temperature' slider (20-200°C) that changes the color tint of both models from blue-cool to red-hot using emissive material properties. (4) A 'Start Titration' button that triggers a 5-second animation where the abalone orbits around the helmet while particles intensify, and both models pulse with emissive glow. (5) A 'Neutralize' button that resets pH to 7 with a smooth animated transition restoring original material properties. (6) A 'Scan Analysis' button that raycasts onto either model on click, displaying a floating HTML tooltip showing fabricated chemical composition data (e.g., CaCO3 percentage for shell, Fe2O3 for helmet). Validate that titration cannot start unless concentration is above 25% and temperature is above 50°C, showing a warning message otherwise. Track completed steps in a progress indicator showing 'Experiment Progress: X/6 steps complete'. All parameter changes should animate smoothly over 0.5 seconds using lerp in the render loop.
